{"number":1621,"title":"logs-prune: give retention_days a 10-day default, declare capture-only","body":"Closes #1620

## The problem

`retention_days` was unset in twelve of the fourteen folding members, and unset meant the prune deleted nothing — so the `conversation-logs` branch grew without bound while `logs-prune` reported success every night. `missingbulb/Shepherd` holds **72 commits, 73 captures, 66.9 MB**, none ever pruned. Only ClaudiniteWebsite and EdFringeNow have ever recorded a `done`.

The pack recommended 10 days in prose from the start (`README.md`, `pack.mjs`) and applied it nowhere: "a project that wants the prune active sets `retention_days` itself" described a step no adoption flow asks for and no automation performs.

## The change

`DEFAULT_RETENTION_DAYS = 10` now lives in `prune-logs.mjs`, the pure decision module, and `resolveRetentionDays` is the single policy both readers go through:

| Declared | Resolves to |
|---|---|
| absent | **10 days** (the default) |
| a positive number | that number |
| `0` or negative | prune off — the explicit capture-only opt-out that absence used to express |
| unreadable / not a number | prune off, **unknown never resolves to the default** |

That last row is the point of the three-state reader rather than a `??`. The prune's one failure direction is deleting what it should not, so a declaration the worker cannot parse must not become a licence to delete.

The signal layer (`claudinite-tasks/signals/local.mjs`) is deliberately untouched: it stays keyed by the parameter rather than the pack, so it keeps reporting `null` for "nothing declared it" and the growth-pack policy is applied in the growth pack. The precondition applies the same resolver, so an opted-out repo is declined before it costs a work item.

## Blast radius — this is a production change

On the nightly converge every member picks up a prune that deletes captures older than 10 days, **in one pass, irreversibly**. On Shepherd that is roughly 45 of 73 captures on the first run.

What makes it safe is the property the pack already relies on and states in `extract-from-conversations`: `growth-extract` reads from the oldest end of the branch on every run, against a retention measured in days, so a capture reaches retention having been read. A member that wants the old behaviour declares `retention_days: 0`.

## Validation

- `packs/claudinite-growth/**` + `packs/claudinite-tasks/**`: **1074 pass, 0 fail**. The one remaining failure in my local run, `engine-pack-lane-shims`, reproduces identically on a stashed tree — it is this container's shallow clone ("too shallow to walk origin/main's pack history"), not this change.
- New tests cover the default, the override, the opt-out, unknown-is-not-the-default, and the reader's `undefined` vs `null` split. Two existing tests asserted the old world and were rewritten to assert the new one — including `signal-context.test.mjs`, which now pins the layering in both directions (the signal invents nothing; the task supplies the default).
- Watched the new tests fail on the unimplemented resolver before implementing.
- `check_the_world.mjs` (world scope): **0 blocking**, and none of the 87 advisories are in the files this touches.

## Folders touched

```
packs/claudinite-growth/tasks/logs-prune/
  prune-logs.mjs   adds DEFAULT_RETENTION_DAYS and resolveRetentionDays — the policy, in the pure module
  worker.mjs       readRetentionDays now separates "said nothing" (undefined) from "cannot tell" (null);
                   main resolves, logs which path ran, and declines on unknown
  preconditions.mjs  applies the same resolver, so the opt-out declines before an item is filed

packs/claudinite-growth/
  pack.mjs         version 60902.1 -> 60902.2; the "unset is fail-safe" rationale replaced by the default's
  README.md        the conversation-lifecycle section now documents the default and the declared opt-out

packs/claudinite-tasks/test/
  signal-context.test.mjs  the signal-vs-task layering, plus a wire-level test for the opt-out
```

content.content:
# logs-prune

## Why the declaration reads as it does

Carried over from the declaration's comments when it became `task.json`.

claudinite-growth task: logs-prune — retention on the `conversation-logs`
branch. `agent_model: 'none'` with `code_work: 'node worker.mjs'`: the whole pass
is deterministic code the scheduler runs as a subprocess — no agent, no dispatch
issue, seconds of runtime. The same shape usage-fold already has over the same
branch.

WHY IT IS NOT PART OF growth-extract. Deleting a capture past retention is
arithmetic on dates over an orphan branch — which is why the extract worker had
to spend prose forbidding an agent to merge that branch or rewrite its history.
Coupled to the opus run it also kept that run's precondition carrying a second
arm whose only job was to fire the prune on a quiet repo, so a repo with nothing
to extract still paid an opus dispatch on the nights one log aged out.

WHAT MAKES AGE ENOUGH. The prune used to be coupled to a judgment step — an aged
log got a final pass before deletion — so pruning on the calendar risked deleting
a capture nothing had read. What removes the risk is the extract run's READING
WINDOW, not a per-file handshake between the two tasks: growth-extract reads from
the oldest end of the branch on every run, against a retention measured in days,
so a capture reaches retention having been read. The extract-from-conversations
skill owns that window; this task owns the arithmetic.

The whole contract is this default export; the retention arithmetic it names is
in preconditions.mjs beside it.
A CLOCK crossing a boundary, not repo movement (the term beside this file):
the prune must keep firing on exactly the repos that went quiet.
It opens no PR: its whole write is remove commits on the non-default logs
branch, which is outside the outcome taxonomy (per-project-scheduling DESIGN §1).
One ls-remote, one fetch, one tree read, at most one push — against a branch
whose size retention itself bounds. Seconds. The bound is protection against a
hung network call, not headroom for work, so it sits just past the slowest
plausible fetch rather than at the leash.

input.body:
Closes #1620

## The problem

`retention_days` was unset in twelve of the fourteen folding members, and unset meant the prune deleted nothing — so the `conversation-logs` branch grew without bound while `logs-prune` reported success every night. `missingbulb/Shepherd` holds **72 commits, 73 captures, 66.9 MB**, none ever pruned. Only ClaudiniteWebsite and EdFringeNow have ever recorded a `done`.

The pack recommended 10 days in prose from the start (`README.md`, `pack.mjs`) and applied it nowhere: "a project that wants the prune active sets `retention_days` itself" described a step no adoption flow asks for and no automation performs.

## The change

`DEFAULT_RETENTION_DAYS = 10` now lives in `prune-logs.mjs`, the pure decision module, and `resolveRetentionDays` is the single policy both readers go through:

| Declared | Resolves to |
|---|---|
| absent | **10 days** (the default) |
| a positive number | that number |
| `0` or negative | prune off — the explicit capture-only opt-out that absence used to express |
| unreadable / not a number | prune off, **unknown never resolves to the default** |

That last row is the point of the three-state reader rather than a `??`. The prune's one failure direction is deleting what it should not, so a declaration the worker cannot parse must not become a licence to delete.

The signal layer (`claudinite-tasks/signals/local.mjs`) is deliberately untouched: it stays keyed by the parameter rather than the pack, so it keeps reporting `null` for "nothing declared it" and the growth-pack policy is applied in the growth pack. The precondition applies the same resolver, so an opted-out repo is declined before it costs a work item.

## Canon does not prune

Second commit: canon holds **506 captures across 606 MB**, back to 2026-07-19. The default would delete **338 of them — 381 MB** — on its first run here. Canon is where the extract corpus is worked over most, so it stops running the task via `taskScheduler.disabledTasks`, which the scheduler reads before it instantiates anything. That is the mechanism for "do not run this task"; a retention value would instead have the task run and decide to delete nothing.

## Blast radius — this is a production change

On the nightly converge every member picks up a prune that deletes captures older than 10 days, **in one pass, irreversibly**. On Shepherd that is roughly 45 of 73 captures on the first run.

What makes it safe is the property the pack already relies on and states in `extract-from-conversations`: `growth-extract` reads from the oldest end of the branch on every run, against a retention measured in days, so a capture reaches retention having been read. A member that wants capture-only declares `retention_days: 0`; one that wants no prune at all names it in `disabledTasks`.

## Validation

- growth + tasks + engine suites on the current head: **1666 pass, 0 fail**.
- New tests cover the default, the override, the opt-out, unknown-is-not-the-default, and the reader's `undefined` vs `null` split. Two existing tests asserted the old world and were rewritten — including `signal-context.test.mjs`, which now pins the layering in both directions (the signal invents nothing; the task supplies the default).
- Watched the new tests fail on the unimplemented resolver before implementing.
- `check_the_world.mjs` (world scope): **0 blocking**, none of the advisories in the files this touches.

Rebased twice onto a moving `main`; `task.mjs` became `task.json` under #1636 in between, and this task's three source files (`preconditions.mjs`, `prune-logs.mjs`, `worker.mjs`) carried over unchanged by that migration. Pack version renumbered to **60903.5** each time to sit above what `main` had reached.

## Folders touched

```
packs/claudinite-growth/tasks/logs-prune/
  prune-logs.mjs   adds DEFAULT_RETENTION_DAYS and resolveRetentionDays — the policy, in the pure module
  worker.mjs       readRetentionDays now separates "said nothing" (undefined) from "cannot tell" (null);
                   main resolves, logs which path ran, and declines on unknown
  preconditions.mjs  applies the same resolver, so the opt-out declines before an item is filed

packs/claudinite-growth/
  pack.mjs         the "unset is fail-safe" rationale replaced by the default's

.claudinite-settings.json
  taskScheduler.disabledTasks gains claudinite-growth/logs-prune — canon stops running it

packs/claudinite-tasks/test/
  signal-context.test.mjs  the signal-vs-task layering, plus a wire-level test for the opt-out
```
